key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on chemical composition and addition order: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide helps passivate the surface.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor exposure and mixing sequence could help preserve MXenes during perovskite processing and tune their surface chemistry.
method: Exposed MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track chemical and surface changes.
Applied density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rapid degradation and dissolution with iodine/polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization with methylammonium iodide, without quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Findings concern a model MAPbI3 precursor environment; improved solar-cell efficiency or long-term device stability is not demonstrated in the abstract.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
